body:
- fixes: https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/657

GitHub Actions shipped a new `queue` key under the `concurrency` section to allow pending workflow runs to queue instead of being cancelled.

Allowed values are "max" and "single" (default).
The combination of `queue: max` with `cancel-in-progress: true` is not permitted.


Reference: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency#example-queueing-multiple-pending-runs

Verified this change and shipped a build of it, since it unblocks a gate that cannot otherwise express a documented key. Reporting what the verification found, in case it is useful before merge.

## The change matches the documentation

Checked against the workflow-syntax reference:

- the two values are `single` (default) and `max`, which is what `parse.go` accepts;
- `queue: max` with `cancel-in-progress: true` is refused, which the docs state explicitly;
- the key is documented at the job level as well as the workflow level, and the testdata covers both.

## The diff fails on the current release, and passes here

`testdata/ok/concurrency_queue.yaml` and `testdata/err/concurrency_queue.{yaml,out}` on the `v1.7.12` tag, with the parser change absent:

```
--- FAIL: TestLinterLintOK/concurrency_queue.yaml
    testdata/ok/concurrency_queue.yaml:5:3: unexpected key "queue" for "concurrency" section. expected one of "cancel-in-progress", "group" [syntax-check]
    testdata/ok/concurrency_queue.yaml:13:7: unexpected key "queue" for "concurrency" section. expected one of "cancel-in-progress", "group" [syntax-check]
    testdata/ok/concurrency_queue.yaml:20:7: unexpected key "queue" for "concurrency" section. expected one of "cancel-in-progress", "group" [syntax-check]
--- FAIL: TestLinterLintError/err/concurrency_queue
      want: "test.yaml:5:10: invalid value \"invalid\" for \"queue\" in \"concurrency\" section. valid values are \"max\" and \"single\" [syntax-check]"
      have: "test.yaml:5:3: unexpected key \"queue\" for \"concurrency\" section. expected one of \"cancel-in-progress\", \"group\" [syntax-check]"
```

So the testdata is a real regression test, not a description of behaviour.

## What is still rejected

One key widens; the section does not. Against the built binary:

```
queue: max                              # accepted
queue: single                           # accepted
queu: max                               # rejected: unexpected key "queu" ... expected one of "cancel-in-progress", "group", "queue"
Queue: max                              # rejected: keys are case-sensitive
queue: unlimited                        # rejected: invalid value "unlimited" ... valid values are "max" and "single"
queue: max + cancel-in-progress: true   # rejected: "queue: max" cannot be combined with "cancel-in-progress: true"
```

## Two faces the testdata does not reach

Not objections — two cases I added where the build needed them, offered here in case you want them upstream.

**An expression value.** `parse.go` skips the value check under `!ret.Queue.ContainsExpression()`, and the combination check is guarded the same way, so `queue: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.queue) }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true` passes. That is the right behaviour — GitHub cannot know the value before the expression runs — but nothing pins it, so a later change that drops the guard would go unnoticed. The guard being correct is currently an accident of two separate conditions happening to agree.

**A bad value at the job level.** `parseConcurrency` is shared, so job-level `queue: Max` is already reported identically. Also unpinned, and the one case where a future refactor could plausibly split the two paths.

I also read the combination guard once more for the case it does not cover: `cancel-in-progress: ${{ ... }}` beside a literal `queue: max` is not refused, since the check requires `ret.CancelInProgress.Expression == nil`. That matches the intent — the value is unknown at parse time — so I did not touch it, but it is worth being deliberate about rather than incidental.

## Build

`Nitjsefnie-OSC/actionlint` carries `v1.7.12-queue.1`: the `v1.7.12` tag plus this commit, on the tag rather than `main` so the delta from the published upstream binary is exactly this patch. Eleven archives, the same platforms and asset names as an upstream release, with `sha256sum -c` clean over all of them.

Not a substitute for merging this, and not a reason to hold it: the gate it unblocks moves back to upstream once the key is modelled, and the pin is a version string.

We hit this in production at Noetive. Two of our deploy workflows share a concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress: false`. Under the default `queue: single`, a Terraform run that ended up skipping every job joined the group second and cancelled the deploy that was waiting. The merge landed, and its migration never shipped. That has happened 7 times in under 4 weeks.

`queue: max`, which GitHub added on 2026-05-07 ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-07-github-actions-concurrency-groups-now-allow-larger-queues/)), fixes it, but actionlint 1.7.12 rejects it:

```
unexpected key "queue" for "concurrency" section. expected one of "cancel-in-progress", "group" [syntax-check]
```

actionlint is a required check for us, so for now we carry a narrow `-ignore` for exactly that message, with a pointer to this PR. We'd drop it as soon as this lands in a release. +1 to merging this, and thank you for actionlint.
